learningObjective: Deploy Azure Bastion with the right SKU and subnet, so admins can RDP and SSH to VMs that have no public IP.
engineer: SKUs: Developer, free, shared, one connection at a time, no subnet needed, only in some regions; Basic; Standard, which adds native client support (your own RDP or SSH app), shareable links, more hosts, connecting by IP address and custom ports; Premium, which adds session recording and a private-only option.
What Basic, Standard and Premium need: a subnet named exactly AzureBastionSubnet, /26 or bigger, and a Standard public IP (Premium private-only doesn't need the IP).
Which VMs it reaches: VMs in its own VNet and in peered VNets.
NSG rules: the VMs' NSGs must allow RDP (3389) or SSH (22) from the AzureBastionSubnet range. An NSG on AzureBastionSubnet itself needs a specific set of required rules.
Native client: az network bastion rdp or az network bastion ssh. Needs Standard or Premium, with Native client support turned on.
Cost: per hour for each Bastion, plus outbound data. Extra scale units on Standard or Premium cost more per hour.

example.title: Removing public IPs used for admin
body: Contoso deploys Standard Bastion in the hub VNet and removes every VM's public IP. Admins connect from the portal, or from their laptops with az network bastion ssh.

architectureDecisions: One Bastion in the hub: it reaches the spokes through peering.
Pick the SKU by feature: Standard for native client and shareable links, Premium for session recording.

misconceptions.myth: VMs need public IPs to use Bastion.
misconceptions.reality: No. Bastion reaches them on their private IPs.
No. It must be exactly AzureBastionSubnet.

troubleshooting.cause: The subnet isn't named AzureBastionSubnet, or it's smaller than /26.
Basic SKU, or native client support is off.
troubleshooting.fix: Upgrade to Standard and turn on native client support.

troubleshooting.cause: The VM's NSG blocks RDP or SSH from the Bastion subnet.
troubleshooting.fix: Allow 3389 or 22 from the AzureBastionSubnet range.
